arxiv-2012-03259.title: Connectivity of orientations of 3-edge-connected graphs
arxiv-2012-03259.creator: Florian Hörsch, Zoltán Szigeti
arxiv-2012-03259.description: Abstract We attempt to generalize a theorem of Nash-Williams stating that a graph has a k k -arc-connected orientation if and only if it is 2 ​ k 2k -edge-connected. In a strongly connected digraph we call an arc deletable if its deletion leaves a strongly connected digraph.

arxiv-2101-10885.title: Solitary waves and double layers in complex plasma media
arxiv-2101-10885.creator: A A Mamun a,c and Abdul Mannan a,b
arxiv-2101-10885.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by A A Mamun a,c and Abdul Mannan a,b. A complex plasma medium (containing Cairns nonthermal electron species, adiabatically warm inertial ion species, and stationary positively charged dust (PCD) species (making a plasma system very complex) is considered. The effects of PCD species, nonthermal electron species, and adiabatic ion-temperature on ion-acoustic (IA) solitary waves (SWs) and double layers (DLs) are investigated by the pseudo-potential approach, which is valid for the arbitrary amplitude time-independent SWs and DLs.

arxiv-2403-08047.title: Transition to a weaker Sun: Changes in the solar atmosphere during the decay of the Modern Maximum
arxiv-2403-08047.creator: K. Mursula, A. A. Pevtsov, T. Asikainen, I. Tähtinen, A. R. Yeates
arxiv-2403-08047.description: Abstract The Sun experienced a period of unprecedented activity during the 20th century, now called the Modern Maximum (MM). The decay of the MM after its maximum in cycle 19 has changed the Sun, the heliosphere, and the planetary environments in many ways. However, studies disagree on whether this decay has proceeded synchronously in different solar parameters or not.

arxiv-2406-01881.title: Activity patterns in ring networks of quadratic integrate-and-fire neurons with synaptic and gap junction coupling
arxiv-2406-01881.creator: Oleh E. Omel’chenko, Carlo R. Laing
arxiv-2406-01881.description: Abstract We consider a ring network of quadratic integrate-and-fire neurons with nonlocal synaptic and gap junction coupling. The corresponding neural field model supports solutions such as standing and travelling waves, and also lurching waves. We show that many of these solutions satisfy self-consistency equations which can be used to follow them as parameters are varied.

arxiv-2406-07533.title: Interpreting DESI 2024 BAO: late-time dynamical dark energy or a local effect?
arxiv-2406-07533.creator: Ioannis D. Gialamas, Gert Hütsi, Kristjan Kannike, Antonio Racioppi, Martti Raidal, Martin Vasar, Hardi Veermäe
arxiv-2406-07533.description: Abstract We perform fits to DESI, CMB and supernova data to understand the physical origin of the DESI hint for dynamical dark energy. We find that the parametrization w = w 0 + ( 1 − a ) ​ w a w=w_{0}+(1-a)w_{a} can, misleadingly, hint for a phantom Universe, although quintessence models fit the data well.

arxiv-2407-14055.title: Quantum Hamiltonian Embedding of Images for Data Reuploading Classifiers
arxiv-2407-14055.creator: Peiyong Wang, Casey R. Myers, Lloyd C. L. Hollenberg, Udaya Parampalli
arxiv-2407-14055.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Peiyong Wang, Casey R. Myers, Lloyd C. L. Hollenberg, Udaya Parampalli. When applying quantum computing to machine learning tasks, one of the first considerations is the design of the quantum machine learning model itself. Conventionally, the design of quantum machine learning algorithms relies on the “quantisation” of classical learning algorithms, such as using quantum linear algebra to implement important subroutines of classical algorithms, if not the entire algorithm, seeking to achieve quantum advantage through possible run-time accelerations brought by quantum computing.

arxiv-2502-15474.title: Recent advances in the analysis of the dissipative Aw-Rascle system Thanks: The work of the author was supported by the EPSRC Early Career Fellowship no. EP/V000586/1.
arxiv-2502-15474.creator: \firstname Ewelina \lastname Zatorska
arxiv-2502-15474.description: Abstract . The one-dimensional Aw-Rascle (AR) system has become a cornerstone of macroscopic models for single-lane vehicular traffic. A possible generalization of this model to a multi-dimensional setting is the so-called dissipative AR model, which is more suited to capturing crowd dynamics.

arxiv-2505-06969.title: Non-decreasable K K -types are unitarily small
arxiv-2505-06969.creator: Chao-Ping Dong, Chengyu Du, Haojun Xu
arxiv-2505-06969.description: Abstract . Let G G be a connected simple non-compact real reductive Lie group with a maximal compact subgroup K K . This note aims to show that any non-decreasable K K -type (in the sense of the first named author) is unitarily small (in the sense of Salamanca-Riba and Vogan). This answers Conjecture 2.

arxiv-2508-02670.title: atommovr: An open-source simulation framework for rearrangement in atomic arrays
arxiv-2508-02670.creator: Nikhil K. Harle, Bo-Yu Chen, Bob Bao, Hannes Bernien
arxiv-2508-02670.description: Abstract The task of atom rearrangement has emerged in the last decade as a fundamental building block for the development of neutral atom-based quantum processors. However, despite many recent efforts to develop algorithms with favorable asymptotic scaling, no time-optimal algorithm has been developed for any rearrangement task.

pmc-11456868.title: A suspensory fixation technique for calcaneal tuberosity avulsion fractures using the TightRope Attachable Button System
pmc-11456868.creator: Gopikrishnan S Nair, Nima Razii, Ting Y Tan, Robert L Carter, Stuart W Bell
pmc-11456868.description: Displaced avulsion fractures of the calcaneal tuberosity generally occur as a result of osteoporotic insufficiency or high-energy injuries. Conventional methods of fixation may be complicated by wound breakdown, metalwork failure, or symptomatic hardware. This is particularly relevant in elderly patients and those with comorbidities, including osteoporosis or diabetes.

pmc-11643459.title: Meta-Analysis of Materials and Treatments Used in Ophthalmic Lenses: Implications for Lens Characteristics
pmc-11643459.creator: Clara Martinez-Perez, Ana Paula Oliveira
pmc-11643459.description: Purpose: This meta-analysis evaluates the evolution, applications, and recent advancements in the materials and treatments used in ophthalmic lenses, focusing on their effectiveness, comfort, and safety, while also considering sustainability as a key factor. Methods: The study was registered with PROSPERO and conducted following the PRISMA and AMSTAR-2 guidelines.

pmc-12666152.title: Second-event endpoints (EFS2, PRFS2 and PFS2) after anti-PD-(L)1-based RCTs: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12666152.creator: Pablo Jimenez-Labaig, Oriol Mirallas, Ana Isabel Martin-Quesada, Antonio Rullan, Dario Trapani, Teresa Amaral, Enriqueta Felip, Josep Tabernero, Kevin J Harrington
pmc-12666152.description: BackgroundImmune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), particularly anti-PD-(L)1s, have transformed cancer care by their extended efficacy, even receiving next-line. Event-free survival 2 (EFS2), progression/recurrence-free survival 2 (PRFS2) and progression-free survival 2 (PFS2) capture the time from randomization to objective recurrence/progression or death on the first subsequent therapy, potentially offering a more accurate measure of durable benefit than first-event endpoints.

pmc-13048546.title: The broad societal value of pembrolizumab for women’s cancer in Canada
pmc-13048546.creator: Elizabeth Brook, Karl Patterson, Nishini Wijenayake, Matthew Madin-Warburton, Kathryn Mishkin, Marie-Claude Meilleur, Annabelle Davies, Kate Young
pmc-13048546.description: AimsThe impact of women’s cancers is multifaceted, with broad societal and economic consequences. Health technology assessments often rely solely on costs and outcomes directly relevant to the healthcare system. Our study incorporates the additional and novel value elements across three perspectives for pembrolizumab in four women’s cancers in a Canadian setting.

pmc-13388086.title: Guarding serenity in the digital age: mindfulness as a buffer against social media-induced psychological discomfort in older tourists
pmc-13388086.creator: Shanping Hu, Boyu Liang
pmc-13388086.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionWhile social media enriches senior tourists’ travel experiences, its psychological adverse impacts remain understudied. Existing literature mainly focuses on youth social media fatigue or older adults’ physical digital divide. Rooted in Conservation of Resources (COR) theory, this study fills the research gap by exploring the internal psychological mechanisms of Social Media-Induced Travel Anxiety (SMITA), its linkage with resource loss and seniors’ serenity, and the moderating effect of mindfulness.MethodsA quantitative cross-sectional design was adopted.

pmc-13467563.title: Prognostic Significance of the CALM Index in Surgically Resected Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
pmc-13467563.creator: Soomin An, Wankyu Eo, Sookyung Lee, Dae Hyun Kim
pmc-13467563.description: Background: Anatomical staging is often insufficient for predicting outcomes in stage I-IIIA non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients after curative resection due to inherent prognostic variability. In this study, we evaluated the prognostic value of the C-reactive protein–albumin–lymphocyte–monocyte (CALM) index as an integrative biomarker for overall survival (OS). Methods: This retrospective study included 533 patients with stage I-IIIA NSCLC.

pmc-13521535.title: Enhancing deep learning-based dental caries detection through feature pyramid network-based image segmentation
pmc-13521535.creator: Maya Fitria, Maulisa Oktiana, Muhammad Aditya Yufnanda, Muhammad Keysha Al-Yassar, Nova Rosdiana, Kahlil Muchtar
pmc-13521535.description: Context:Dental caries is a multifactorial disease that may lead to pain, infection, and tooth loss if left untreated, and it requires early detection to prevent complications and to reduce costs. Advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has enabled automated caries detection using intraoral images.

pmc-13525658.title: Conserved protein folds underpin the diversification of secreted proteins in a fungal pathogen
pmc-13525658.creator: Thaís C. S. Dal’Sasso, Eva H. Stukenbrock
pmc-13525658.description: BackgroundDuring host colonization, fungal plant pathogens secrete effector-like proteins that alter host cell physiology and target plant-associated microbes. However, rapid evolution and low sequence conservation hinder the study and characterization of these proteins. The fungus Zymoseptoria passerinii infects Hordeum spp. and includes lineages adapted to wild and domesticated barley.

uslaw-usc-t20-s130aa3.title: 20 U.S.C. § 130aa–3 — Withdrawals and expenditures
uslaw-usc-t20-s130aa3.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t20-s130aa3.description: United States Code, Title 20 (Education); Chapter 8 (Howard University); Subchapter II (Endowment). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Defrayment of expenses; restrictions on use of income or corpus; limits on withdrawals or expenditures The University may withdraw and expend its endowment fund income to defray any expenses necessary to its operation, including expenses of operations and maintenance, administration, academic and support.
